func connects(grid [][]byte, player byte, start, goal func(r, c int) bool) bool {
	rows := len(grid)
	visited := make([][]bool, rows)
	queue := [][2]int{}
	for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
		visited[r] = make([]bool, len(grid[r]))
		for c := 0; c < len(grid[r]); c++ {
			if grid[r][c] == player && start(r, c) {
				visited[r][c] = true
				queue = append(queue, [2]int{r, c})
			}
		}
	}
	for len(queue) > 0 {
		r, c := queue[0][0], queue[0][1]
		queue = queue[1:]
		if goal(r, c) {

}

package connect

import (
	"errors"
)

// ResultOf determines the winner of a game of Hex / Polygon.
//
// The board is given as a slice of strings, one per row, with spaces
// already stripped. Each row is indented (in the original representation)
// one half-cell further than the row above it, which gives the hexagonal
// adjacency used below.
//
// Player "O" wins by connecting the top and bottom edges of the board.
// Player "X" wins by connecting the left and right edges of the board.
// If neither player has such a connection, the empty string is returned.
func ResultOf(lines []string) (string, error) {
	if len(lines) == 0 {
		return "", nil
	}

	grid := make([][]byte, len(lines))
	for r, line := range lines {
		grid[r] = []byte(line)
	}

	xWins := connects(grid, 'X',
		func(r, c int) bool { return c == 0 },
		func(r, c int) bool { return c == len(grid[r])-1 },
	)
	oWins := connects(grid, 'O',
		func(r, c int) bool { return r == 0 },
		func(r, c int) bool { return r == len(grid)-1 },
	)

	switch {
	case xWins && oWins:
		return "", errors.New("both players have a winning connection")
	case xWins:
		return "X", nil
	case oWins:
		return "O", nil
	default:
		return "", nil
	}
}

// connects reports whether player has a connected path of its stones from
// any cell satisfying start to any cell satisfying goal.
func connects(grid [][]byte, player byte, start, goal func(r, c int) bool) bool {
	rows := len(grid)
	visited := make([][]bool, rows)
	var queue [][2]int

	for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
		visited[r] = make([]bool, len(grid[r]))
		for c := 0; c < len(grid[r]); c++ {
			if grid[r][c] == player && start(r, c) {
				visited[r][c] = true
				queue = append(queue, [2]int{r, c})
			}
		}
	}

	for len(queue) > 0 {
		cur := queue[0]
		queue = queue[1:]
		r, c := cur[0], cur[1]
		if goal(r, c) {
			return true
		}
		for _, n := range neighbors(r, c) {
			nr, nc := n[0], n[1]
			if nr < 0 || nr >= rows || nc < 0 || nc >= len(grid[nr]) {
				continue
			}
			if visited[nr][nc] || grid[nr][nc] != player {
				continue
			}
			visited[nr][nc] = true
			queue = append(queue, [2]int{nr, nc})
		}
	}
	return false
}

// neighbors returns the six hexagonal neighbours of cell (r, c).
// Each row is shifted half a cell to the right relative to the row above,
// so the cells diagonally up-left / up-right and down-left / down are
// adjacent.
func neighbors(r, c int) [][2]int {
	return [][2]int{
		{r - 1, c},     // up-left
		{r - 1, c + 1}, // up-right
		{r, c - 1},     // left
		{r, c + 1},     // right
		{r + 1, c - 1}, // down-left
		{r + 1, c},     // down
	}
}
